The Social Security Administration’s chronic delays and bureaucratic inertia are exactly why accountability matters. While constituent services can resolve individual cases, systemic failures demand structural reform. The Department of Government Efficiency has already clawed back $165B through contract cancellations and grant terminations—including slashing $367M from HHS refugee resettlement contracts and $1.75B from GAVI Foundation global health grants. Yet SSA’s own $826B budget in FY2024 still hemorrhages taxpayer funds into dysfunction.

Real solutions require dismantling legacy systems that prioritize paperwork over people. The 2024 Congressional Inquiries Guide proves SSA’s processes are stuck in the 20th century, with 1M+ disability claims backlogged and 30,000 Americans dying annually waiting for decisions.

Efficiency isn’t about bandaids—it’s about rebuilding agencies from the ground up with zero tolerance for waste. Until Washington stops rubber-stamping SSA’s status quo, constituents will keep needing rescue missions from their representatives.

While AI could streamline diagnostics and reduce $375B in annual administrative bloat, current policies prioritize subsidizing tech contracts over dismantling cartels that inflate drug costs 300% above production. Real reform requires exposing how 25% of healthcare spending gets lost in bureaucratic black holes while patients face rationed care.

AI should target Medicare fraud and $60B in improper payments first—not serve as another slush fund for D.C.'s contractor buddies.
